2.5 Embedded Image Display

Displaying bitmap images compiled directly into the firmware using LVGL’s image system.

Overview

LVGL can display images stored as C arrays in program memory. This project shows how to embed a static image (the “StarryNight” painting) into firmware and display it on screen — a technique useful for splash screens, icons, and backgrounds.

What You’ll Learn

  • Converting images to LVGL-compatible C arrays using the online LVGL Image Converter

  • Creating an LVGL image object (lv_img)

  • Declaring and using lv_img_dsc_t image descriptors

How the Code Works

Image Data

The image is converted to a C file (StarryNight.c) containing a pixel array and descriptor:

const lv_img_dsc_t StarryNight = {
    .header.cf = LV_IMG_CF_TRUE_COLOR,
    .header.always_zero = 0,
    .header.reserved = 0,
    .header.w = 240,
    .header.h = 320,
    .data_size = 240 * 320 * 2,
    .data = starrynight_map,
};

Displaying

lv_obj_t *img = lv_img_create(lv_scr_act());
lv_img_set_src(img, &StarryNight);

Expected Result

A 240×320 full-screen image of “StarryNight” is displayed on the TFT screen with a caption “Starry Night” at the bottom.

Note

Large images consume significant flash memory. For the 16MB flash variant, this is not an issue. For production projects, consider loading images from the SD card (see 2.8 SD Card Photo Gallery).
